scenes.narration: Hello, my little friends! Do you know who the first two women were who led an army to chase away invaders and win back the land for the Viet people? Today, Huy Tells Tales will tell you the story of how the Trung Sisters rose up.

Once upon a time, almost two thousand years ago, our country was ruled by the Han people from the faraway north. The Han officials made our people hand over lots and lots of rice and silk. The Viet people had a very hard life.

In Me Linh district, between Ba Vi Mountain and Tam Dao Mountain, there lived two sisters named Trung Trac and Trung Nhi. Their father was a Lac lord, a descendant of the Hung kings, but he had passed away young. Trung Nhi (happily): "Sister, our silkworms have spun golden silk all over the whole tray!" Trung Trac (happily): "You are so clever with your hands. Tomorrow we will weave silk as a gift for Mother."

The sisters' mother was Lady Man Thien. She raised her children all by herself. She taught her two daughters to grow mulberry trees and raise silkworms, and she taught them martial arts too. Lady Man Thien (firmly): "My dear children, learn to weave silk so you can take care of yourselves, and learn to hold a spear so you can protect your village." Trung Trac (firmly): "Yes, Mother! We will always remember your words!"

Every morning on the riverside field, the two sisters practiced martial arts hard. The sound of their wooden spears clacking together rang out, clack, clack. Trung Nhi (laughing): "Sister, can you block this spear move of mine?" Trung Trac (laughing): "You are very quick, but I am even quicker than you!"

At that time, the Han court sent an official named To Dinh to be the governor of Giao Chi. He was greedy and cruel. To Dinh (shouting): "Every home must hand over more rice and more silk to me!" Old Man (worried): "Sir, this year the harvest failed. The people have nothing left to give." To Dinh (angrily): "If you don't pay, I will send you all away to do forced labor!"

That was not all. The Han soldiers also made the Viet people give up their wedding customs and the clothes of their grandparents, and follow the Han ways instead. Han Soldier (shouting): "From now on, everyone must follow the rules of the Han people!" Old Woman (sadly): "These customs were handed down by our ancestors for ages. Oh heavens, how can they make us give them up?"

Trung Trac and Trung Nhi traveled through the villages. Seeing the people suffer, they felt great sorrow. The two sisters were strong by nature, and they would not bow to To Dinh's harsh laws. Trung Trac (angrily): "To Dinh has bullied our people far too much!" Trung Nhi (firmly): "Sister, we cannot sit still any longer!"

When she grew up, Trung Trac married Thi Sach, the son of a Lac lord in Chu Dien district, right across the Day River. Thi Sach was a brave and mighty man. Thi Sach (firmly): "My dear wife, our two families share the same goal, and we both care for the good people." Trung Trac (firmly): "I promise to protect our homeland together with you."

The two families quietly joined hands with Lac lords everywhere. Lady Man Thien also went to meet the chiefs around the region. Lady Man Thien (firmly): "We are the children and grandchildren of the Hung kings. How can we bow our heads forever?" Many chiefs nodded and promised to rise up together.

The news reached To Dinh. He feared the Viet people would rise up, so he did something cruel. To Dinh (shouting): "Thi Sach dares to stand against me. Seize him at once!" And so, Thi Sach was killed by To Dinh.

Hearing the terrible news, Trung Trac was heartbroken. Trung Trac (crying): "My husband, oh my husband!" But then she wiped away her tears and looked out at the river. Trung Trac (firmly): "I will surely avenge my family and win back my country!"

The two sisters led their troops to the mouth of the Hat River to get ready. Villagers eagerly came to forge spears, carve arrows, and make crossbows. Old Man (happily): "I am old but still strong. Let me forge spears for the Two Ladies to fight the invaders!" Trung Nhi (happily): "Thank you, Grandfather! When the whole village works together, any enemy will be afraid."

Something special happened. Many women came to join the Two Ladies, such as Le Chan, Thanh Thien, and Bat Nan. Every one of them was skilled in martial arts and brave. Le Chan (firmly): "We women also know how to hold a spear and defend our country!" Trung Trac (joyfully): "With you, my sisters, my heart is as steady as Ba Vi Mountain."

On the fourth day of the ninth month, on the rocky shore at the mouth of the Hat River, the Two Ladies gathered the generals for a solemn oath. Flags fluttered and everyone stood straight and proud. Trung Trac (firmly): "First, I vow to wash away the shame of our enemies!" Trung Trac (firmly): "Second, I vow to rebuild the old kingdom of the Hung kings!"

Trung Trac (firmly): "Third, I cry out for justice for my husband. Fourth, I vow to finish this great task completely!" Their vow echoed across the whole river. The Rebels (shouting): "We vow to drive out the Han invaders!" Trung Nhi (shouting): "We vow to win back our homeland!"

In the spring of the year forty, the day to march out had come. Trung Trac was still in mourning for her husband, but she wore a beautiful gown and combed her hair neatly, and she stood shining before the army. Le Chan (surprised): "Sister, you are still in mourning for your husband. Why are you dressed so beautifully today?"

Trung Trac (firmly): "Fighting the invaders cannot wait. If I looked gloomy, the soldiers would lose their spirit. I dress beautifully so our army shines even brighter, and the enemy will tremble when they see us!" The generals all listened and admired her. Le Chan (proudly): "You truly deserve to lead us, Sister!"

Boom, boom, boom! The bronze drums rang out. The army of the Two Ladies marched forward with a rumble, their spears gleaming in the sunshine. Trung Nhi (shouting): "Brothers and sisters, forward!" The Rebels (shouting): "Drive out To Dinh!"

In the first battle, the rebels attacked the enemy fort at Me Linh. The Han soldiers did not even have time to pick up their spears before they were in a panic. Han Soldier (scared): "The Two Ladies' army is here! Run away quickly!" The enemy fell over and scattered in all directions. The Me Linh fort was won by the rebels.

After the victory, the Two Ladies marched on Co Loa Citadel. The people there opened the gates and came out with food and water to welcome them. Old Woman (joyfully): "The Two Ladies are here, everyone!" Trung Trac (happily): "Do not be afraid, good people. We have come to drive the invaders away for you!"

From Co Loa, the rebels rowed their boats across the river and attacked Luy Lau, where To Dinh had his headquarters. Trung Nhi (shouting): "Sister, Luy Lau Citadel is right in front of us!" Trung Trac (firmly): "Forward! We will not let To Dinh escape!"

Inside the headquarters, To Dinh shook with fear. The Two Ladies' army struck as fast as the wind, and he had no time to fight back. To Dinh (scared): "How did their army get here so fast?" Han Soldier (scared): "Sir, the city gate is about to break!"

Afraid of being recognized, To Dinh quickly shaved his head, shaved off his beard, and even threw away his official seal. To Dinh (scared): "Shave off all my beard and hair! Throw this seal away too. Let's run!" The once bossy official hid among the soldiers and ran away with his head down. He looked so funny.
To Dinh ran all the way back to Nam Hai, in the land of the Han. Later, even the Han emperor scolded him for being greedy and cowardly, and he was thrown into prison.

News of the victory flew far and wide. The people of Cuu Chan, Nhat Nam, and Hop Pho all rose up to join in. Before long, the Two Ladies had won back sixty-five citadels. Old Man (joyfully): "The invaders have all run away! Our homeland belongs to us Viet people again!"

The Lac lords together honored Trung Trac as queen. She set up her capital at Me Linh, and Trung Nhi became Vice Queen to help her sister. Le Chan (shouting): "We ask that Sister Trung Trac be crowned queen!" The Rebels (shouting): "Long live Queen Trung!"

Queen Trung stood before all the people, her voice warm yet carrying far. Trung Trac (proudly): "From now on, our people may live by the customs of our grandparents. I give thanks to our ancestors, the Hung kings." Trung Nhi (firmly): "I promise to stay with you, Sister, and keep our land safe!"

For more than three years, the Viet people ruled their homeland themselves. After that, the Han court sent a general named Ma Vien with a huge army to attack. Trung Trac (firmly): "Even if the enemy is many, we sisters will never bow our heads!" Trung Nhi (firmly): "I will always be by your side!" The Two Ladies fought to the very end at Cam Khe, then rose up to heaven beside the Hat River, leaving a shining example that lasts for all time.

Today, beside the Hat River, there is still the Hat Mon Temple to honor the Two Ladies. Nearby is Ha Loi village, their mother's hometown, and Men Shrine, which honors Lady Man Thien, the mother of the Two Ladies. The history books call Trung Trac the Trung Queen, and the people lovingly call the Two Ladies the Two Saints of Me Linh. People still come to light incense and remember the great deeds of these two heroes.

My dear little friends, the Trung Sisters show us that girls are brave and talented too, just as much as anyone. Let us love our homeland, care for everyone, and stay united together, all right? If you liked this story, please remember to subscribe to the channel Huy Kể Chuyện to hear many more fun stories from Vietnamese history. See you again soon!
